question.worked_solution:
Notice that we can rewrite the given sum as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{50}+\frac{1}{375}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n{5}^{n}}+⋯= \\ (\frac{1}{5})-\frac{(1/5)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(1/5)^{3}}{3}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(1/5)^{n}}{n}+⋯ & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{1}{5}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1\,+\,\frac{1}{5}) & =(\frac{1}{5})-\frac{(1/5)^{2}}{2}+\frac{(1/5)^{3}}{3}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(1/5)^{n}}{n}+⋯ \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{6}{5}) & =\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{25\cdot 2}+\frac{1}{125\cdot 3}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(1/5)^{n}}{n}+⋯ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{50}+\frac{1}{375}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n{5}^{n}}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{6}{5}).$
